newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Military officials based in the Autonomous Region in Moslem Mindanao have started mediating between two warring groups of the Moro National Liberation Front in Sulu in an effort to defuse the tension in the region. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- More overseas Filipino workers are clamouring for the early passage of the absentee voting bills which they said had been ignored by both the houses of Congress. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- A key Malacanang adviser yesterday confirmed there were indeed moves to initiate amendments to the Constitution but said none of the leaders of the ruling party had anything to do with these. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The Senate committee on agriculture and food is gearing up to probe the government's reported excess importation of rice, five million bags of which were reportedly found rotting in the National Food Authority's warehouse. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)

- A visiting team from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has expressed satisfaction on the overall performance of the Philippine economy despite concerns on the balance of payments data and the swelling trade deficit. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)
- San Miguel has entered into a licensing agreement with American brewer Miller Brewing Co to produce and distribute Miller Genuine Draft in the Philippines.
